objective.statement: Know the Italian words that tell you how fast to play.
successCriteria: I know a tempo word at the start of a piece tells the player the speed.
I know allegro is fast, andante is walking pace and adagio is slow.
I can match a tempo word to its meaning.

explanation.text: Tempo means speed. At the start of a piece, a word often tells the player how fast the music should go. Many of these words are Italian, because Italian was the language of music for centuries.

music.textAlternative: A treble stave with the word Allegro written above it.

explanation.text: From slow to fast, the words you need are: adagio and lento (slow), andante (at a walking pace), moderato (at a moderate speed), allegretto (fairly quick) and allegro (fast and lively).
Andante is the walking word. Its root is the Italian verb 'andare', which means 'to go', so think of music that goes along at an easy, steady walk.

music.textAlternative: Four rising crotchets, C D E F, with the word Andante above the stave.

steps: Press Play all. The notes are played at one steady speed.
Imagine the same notes marked Adagio: slow and calm.
And now Allegro: quick and bright. The notes are the same; only the speed changes.
demonstration.textAlternative: Four rising notes marked Andante. The word tells the player how fast to take them.

options.label: fairly quick, but not as fast as allegro

feedback.correct: Yes: a tempo word is about speed.
